stem: Using npv(rate, cfs), which discounts cash flow i by (1 + rate)**i starting at i = 0, what is npv(0.10, [-500, 200, 200, 200])?
explanation: The investment of −500 is at t = 0 and is not discounted. The three 200 inflows are worth 181.82 + 165.29 + 150.26 = 497.37, so NPV = −2.63.

rationale.B: Incorrect. 100.00 simply adds the cash flows without discounting.
rationale.C: Incorrect. −2.39 discounts every cash flow one period too many (exponents starting at 1), which also discounts the initial outlay.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 497.37 is the PV of the inflows only; the initial investment of 500 was left out.

verify: const cf=[-500,200,200,200]; let s=0; for(let t=0;t<cf.length;t++){s+=cf[t]/Math.pow(1.1,t);} return s;

stem: bond_price(100, 0.04, 0.06, 2, freq=2) prices a 2-year bond with a 4% annual coupon paid semiannually at a 6% annual yield. The result is closest to:
explanation: Per half-year: coupon 2, yield 3%, 4 periods. Price = 2/1.03 + 2/1.03² + 2/1.03³ + 102/1.03⁴ = 96.28.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 96.33 is the annual-pay price (coupon 4, yield 6%, 2 periods); the frequency was ignored.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 86.14 halves the coupon and doubles the periods but discounts at the full 6% per half-year instead of 3%.
rationale.C: Correct. Divide coupon and yield by 2 and use 4 periods: 96.28.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 103.81 swaps the coupon and yield (a 6% coupon priced at a 4% yield); with a coupon below the yield the bond must trade below par.

verify: let p=0; for(let k=1;k<=4;k++){p+=2/Math.pow(1.03,k);} p+=100/Math.pow(1.03,4); return p;

stem: An analyst calls brentq(lambda r: npv(r, cfs), 0.20, 0.50) to find an IRR and gets a ValueError. The most likely cause is:
options: NPV has the same sign at 20% and 50%, so the interval does not bracket a root
npv must be vectorised with np.vectorize before brentq can use it
brentq cannot solve for rates above 10%
explanation: Brent's method needs f(lo) and f(hi) to have opposite signs. If the IRR is below 20%, NPV is negative at both 20% and 50%, and brentq refuses to start.

rationale.A: Incorrect. brentq works with any real-valued bounds.
rationale.B: Correct. Without a sign change in the bracket there is no guaranteed root, so brentq raises a ValueError.
rationale.C: Incorrect. brentq calls the function with one scalar at a time; no vectorisation is needed.
rationale.D: Incorrect. There is no such limit; the bracket simply has to contain the root.

stem: A bond priced at 95 has a modified duration of 7.2. Using the duration approximation, the price change for a 0.5 percentage-point rise in yield is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. −0.34 uses Δy = 0.0005 (5 basis points) instead of 0.005.
rationale.B: Incorrect. −34.20 uses Δy = 0.05, i.e. 5 percentage points.
rationale.C: Incorrect. −3.60 is the percentage change (7.2 × 0.5%) read as a price change without multiplying by the price of 95.
